legal_line: Schreiber AI is a Schreiber Holding LLC company.
secondary_tagline: Bringing AI back to every business.

colors._note: Rev 1 keys kept so existing code keeps working; each now carries the v2 value for the same job. graphite=S0 page, slate=S1 sections, panel=S2 panels, text=Paper, muted=Fog, cyan=Signal Blue (accent/links), amber=Hold yellow (caution; Rev 1 used amber for caution — the v2 amber is reserved for the primary button, see button_amber), red=Stop, green=Run, light_bg=Shop White, light_text=Ink.

rules: Schreiber AI is the only customer-facing brand. Write the product line as "BEN Engine, by Schreiber AI". The holding company appears only in the legal line: "Schreiber AI is a Schreiber Holding LLC company."

Use the v2 masters from brand/v2 (mark, horizontal lockup, stacked lockup, small marks). Never redraw, retype, stretch or recolor them. Signal mark on dark, Deep Cobalt mark on white. Below 48 px use the small mark.
The mark says "Ai"; the wordmark and all copy say "AI".
One job per color. Safety Amber is the primary button only, one per screen, text on amber is Night Navy. Headline highlights are Signal Blue, never amber.
Status colors (Run, Hold, Stop, Info) are for status chips and alarms only, never brand.
Heat maps and hot/cold aisles use the thermal ramp (#5CD6FF cool to #FF8A3D warm) with a legend.
Every piece carries the data plate band: Schreiber AI · BEN Engine · <tier> · S/N · Rated kW IT · voltage · IP · Rev 2.

Product name is written BEN Engine. Tiers are BEN 1, BEN 5, BEN 30, BEN 150, BEN 300, BEN 500, BEN 1000, BEN 2000 (the number is the nominal maximum IT kW). Outdoor enclosures are NEMA 4X / IP66 with hardening H1/H2/H3; never the rain-only 3R rating.
Numbers come from the configuration model or measured evidence. No invented metrics. An empty proof slot is a yellow 'fact pending' chip.
Samples and previews sent to prospects are watermarked Schreiber AI.
